findings.problem: The direction's signature gesture breaks the direction's central promise on its first click. Driven at 1440: invitations sits at 23 days / top 322px; one press of “Move a week earlier” puts it at 16 days / top 224px — the exact pixel already held by the menu tasting (16 days, top 224px). Both titles overstrike into an unreadable smear (screenshot captured), two rows share one count in the gutter, and nothing re-sorts: data-lead stays on the menu tasting, the gap note still reads “Nothing is planned for the next 16 days”, and my collision probe returns two hits where interaction-check.mjs asserted zero. That gate is not silent about this — it performs precisely this click (line 293) and only asserts that OTHER items did not move, so a defect the lock calls impossible (“no two items can collide at any width”) is escorted past by its own guard. move() also has no upper clamp: fourteen presses of +7 put the item at 100 days / top 1400px, 580px below the wedding day and 202px outside the measure's own inline height of 1198px, still drawing.
findings.fix: In render-b.js, replace the direct style.top write in move() with a place(measureEl, px) function that re-runs after every change: (1) read each item's days-away from data-away (defaulting to its fixture value), (2) clamp the edited value to 1..F.toDay(), (3) sort ascending and set data-lead on the nearest only, (4) walk nearest-first and merge any item whose top is within the previous item's measured offsetHeight into that previous item as a second title inside the same .b-item — one tick, one count, titles stacked, since two things on the same day is a real wedding, not an error — and (5) write style.top from the clamped value. Call place() once at render and once per move. Then add to interaction-check.mjs, inside the existing primary-gesture block and repeated at 390 / 901 / 1440: after one −7 click and after ten +7 clicks, assert zero collisions among .b-measure .b-item, assert every item's bottom is inside .b-measure's box, and assert exactly one [data-lead="true"] and that it is the nearest item by count.

findings.problem: After one −7 click the same milestone states four different facts on one screen, three of them false. Read from the live DOM: .b-away = “16”, .b-date = “Sat 8 Aug” (unchanged), the grab button's accessible name = “Send the invitations, Saturday 8 August, in 23 days. Shown to guests” (unchanged), and .b-stepRead = “in 16 days”. move() writes the count and the pixel and nothing else, so the only surface that knows the new position is the count column, and the readout — which opened as “Saturday 8 August 2026 · in 23 days” — drops the calendar date entirely the moment you touch it: the owner is moving a wedding milestone and the screen stops telling them which date they have landed on. This is the paid-for “self-contradicting counts” and “one grammar per fact” class, reintroduced by the one interaction this direction exists for. The gate's assertion “both readouts agree after a move” compares the readout with .b-away only, so it passes while the date line and the accessible name are stale. Separately, the .b-undo live region ships pre-written as “Last change: the invitations moved seven days closer” before any change has been made, and never updates after one.
findings.fix: Add to fixture.js an accessor addDays: function (iso, n) { var d = new Date(utc(iso) + n * 86400000); return d.toISOString().slice(0, 10); }. In render-b.js move(), derive var iso = F.addDays(target.date, current - away) and from that one value rewrite, in the same frame: .b-away = String(current); .b-date = F.fmt.weekdayShort(iso) + " " + F.fmt.short(iso); the .b-grab aria-label = target.title + ", " + F.fmt.long(iso) + ", in " + current + " days. Shown to guests. Open to change it."; and read.textContent = F.fmt.longYear(iso) + " · in " + current + " days" so the calendar date never disappears. Set the .b-undo sentence from the same move ("Last change: " + target.title + " moved " + Math.abs(delta) + " days " + (delta < 0 ? "closer" : "further away") + ".") and render it empty until the first move. Add to interaction-check.mjs: after a move, assert .b-date, the grab aria-label and .b-stepRead all name the date implied by .b-away, and that .b-undo is empty before any interaction.

findings.element: b.css @media (max-width: 700px) blocks at lines 35-40 and 117-127, plus .b-print at line 627
findings.problem: Fifteen declarations written to make this work on a phone have no effect at any width, because every one of them is a bare class (0,1,0) fighting [data-medium="full"] .x / [data-medium="sheet"] .x (0,2,0) written earlier in the same file — and a media query adds no specificity. Measured at 390px on owner-flight, owner-editing, owner-empty, publish, desk and print: .b-field padding computes to 48px 56px 56px (the desk value, 29% of a 390px screen in side padding) directly under the comment “A desk padding on a phone is a quarter of the screen”; .b-measure padding-left 124px; .b-item left 124px; .b-title 24px; .b-num 148px; owner-empty's headline 64px with 120px/56px padding. The two exceptions prove the same rule from the other side: .b-ended's phone padding loses on source order instead (computed 72px 22px 80px, not the 56/22/64 in the block), and .b-print's own page margins never apply at any width (computed 48px 56px 56px at 1440 as well as 390). The consequences are not cosmetic: at 390 the owner measure has 154px left for a 24px title, so “Menu tasting at The Orchard” renders as “Menu tasting at The…” and the “shown” chip of each row lands on the next row's title — my collision probe returns three overlaps of 12px at 390 and the same three at 901, in the two-column band the gate never measures (it checks collisions at 1440 for owner-flight and at 390 only for phone).
findings.fix: In b.css, give the phone block the specificity it needs by prefixing every selector in both @media (max-width: 700px) blocks with [data-medium] — [data-medium] .b-field, [data-medium] .b-empty, [data-medium] .b-ended, [data-medium] .b-print, [data-medium] .b-measure, [data-medium] .b-rail, [data-medium] .b-item, [data-medium] .b-away, [data-medium] .b-tick, [data-medium] .b-item[data-lead="true"] .b-tick, [data-medium] .b-item[data-anchor="true"]::before, [data-medium] .b-measureHead, [data-medium] .b-title — and move both blocks to the end of the file so source order can never re-open the .b-ended case. Change .b-print's padding rule to .b-print.b-field { padding: 56px 64px 44px; } so it outranks [data-medium="sheet"] .b-field. Then extend the phone block to cover what it now actually reaches: [data-medium] .b-num { font-size: 96px } and [data-medium] .b-emptyTitle { font-size: 38px } under 700px. In interaction-check.mjs, run the existing collision probe over states phone, desk, owner-flight, owner-editing and print at 390, 768, 901, 1280 and 1440 rather than at one width each, and add an assertion that no .b-field computes side padding greater than 24px below 700px.

findings.problem: The comment on .b-title says “The clamp is word-safe and keeps the whole string in the accessible name”, but the thing doing the clipping is -webkit-line-clamp: 2 with overflow: hidden, which cuts at the character — the exact class the defect library was paid to close. The JS word-safe clamp cannot reach it: clamp() only ever compares scrollWidth with clientWidth, and a wrapping -webkit-box overflows vertically, so the function returns at its first test and never trims a word. Measured: at 901px on desk and owner-flight, and at 390px on desk, .b-title elements report scrollHeight − clientHeight = 32px — a full line hidden — and the rendered string is “Menu tasting at The…”. Both gates pass on it and neither could fail: interaction-check.mjs's “no clamp cuts mid-word” compares textContent with data-full, which line-clamp never changes, so the filter is always empty; and “no silent text clipping” skips anything whose overflow is vertical.
findings.fix: In b.css, replace the -webkit-box clamp on .b-title with max-height: 2.6em; overflow: hidden; (2 × the 1.3 line-height) and delete display: -webkit-box, -webkit-line-clamp and -webkit-box-orient. In render-core.js clamp(), replace the single early return with a two-axis test: function over(el) { return el.scrollWidth > el.clientWidth + 1 || el.scrollHeight > el.clientHeight + 1; }, return early when !over(el), and drive the existing word-popping loop with while (words.length > 1 && over(el)). Because clamp() already restores from data-full first, the trim stays idempotent across the fonts.ready re-run. In interaction-check.mjs, add: at 390, 901 and 1440 across phone, desk, owner-flight and print, assert every [data-clamp] element has scrollHeight <= clientHeight + 1 and scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 1, and that any element whose textContent differs from its data-full ends in a whole word plus an ellipsis.

findings.element: render-b.js measure() role="list" (line 94), field() aria-label (line 131), horizon() (lines 38-51)
findings.problem: The received artifact — the screen the brief says decides everything — has almost no accessibility tree. Read from the live phone state: the only heading in the document is h2 “Behind you”; the couple's name, the 79, the wedding date and every milestone are plain p and span, so a screen-reader user jumping by heading lands on what is already over and can never reach the day itself. .b-measure carries role="list" and aria-label “What is still ahead, nearest first”, but its eight element children are seven role-less divs and the decorative .b-rail: none is a listitem, so the label sits on a list of zero items and every milestone is orphaned generic text. .b-field carries aria-label “The plan for Mara & Finn” on a div with no role, where it is dropped. And the count column's only unit is the .b-measureHead word “days away”, a paragraph outside the list with no programmatic association, so each row reads as the bare string “16 Menu tasting at The Orchard Sat 1 Aug” — position and a naked number carrying the fact, which is precisely the “state carried only visually” class. The owner states are better served (the grab button names the date in words), which shows this is an omission on the guest surface specifically, not a house style.
findings.fix: In render-b.js: render the project name in horizon() as h("h1.b-who", ...) and add .b-who { font-weight: 400; } to b.css so the two-weight ladder holds; render field() as h("main.b-field" + ...) so its aria-label has a role to attach to; give .b-rail "aria-hidden": "true"; and give every .b-item role: "listitem" plus "aria-label": item.title + ", " + F.fmt.long(item.date) + ", " + away + " days away" (append ", the day itself" when isAnchor and ", the next thing" when it is the lead) so the count, the date and the mark exist in words. Add to interaction-check.mjs, across phone, desk, print and owner-flight: assert exactly one h1 per state and that it names the project; assert .b-measure [role="listitem"] count equals the number of .b-items and that no non-listitem element is a child of the role="list"; assert every item's accessible name contains its own date and the word “days”; and assert no element carries an aria-label without a role or a native semantic.

biggestWin: The measure earns its thesis on load. Every vertical position is daysFromToday × pixels-per-day off the real fixture dates, and I could not make it lie: across phone, desk, owner-flight and print the scale spread between items is under a thousandth of a pixel per day, the horizon count, the last tick and the fixture all read 79, and the seven-day gap between the menu tasting and the invitations measures exactly half the fourteen-day gap above it. The 148px count with a fortnight of real emptiness beneath it is an object I have not seen another product ship, and it survives the ground flip on nine lines of ladder rather than a parallel stylesheet, with print forced to paper and proven so. That composition is 9.5 material; what stands between it and the gate is not taste but mechanics — the interaction that moves an item, the responsive block that never fires, and the accessibility tree of the guest screen. Roughly a day and a half of build in render-b.js, render-core.js and b.css, plus the assertions that would have caught each one; none of it is a different decision.
